title: AMPSDEV-373 Harden archive extraction and Spring Java transform against path traversal
description:
During an internal audit, we looked at AMPS 9.13.0 and found two confirmed issues and a handful of hardening gaps \([AMPSDEV-373](https://ecosystem.atlassian.net/browse/AMPSDEV-373)\). 

Neither is reachable over HTTP, but a malicious archive could write files outside the target directory as the developer or CI user: `atlas-update -Dsdk.archive.path=...` didn't check TAR entries at all \(A-005\), and unpacking a `productDataPath` home ZIP didn't check ZIP entries \(A-006\). The same unchecked `ZipUtils.unzip` sits behind product distributions, bundled plugins and Spring context extraction \(B-171 to B-175\), and the Spring XML to Java transform wrote generated files without confining their paths \(B-176 to B-178\).

This PR closes all of them:

* **Archive extraction** \(`ZipUtils`\) now refuses entries with absolute, drive-letter or UNC names, entries that resolve outside the target directory, and symbolic links, hard links or other special files. Every entry is validated before anything is written, so a refused archive leaves the target directory untouched, and writes never follow existing symbolic links or junctions. `..` segments that stay inside the target are still fine.
* **Spring XML to Java transform** only loads templates by simple name, and refuses to write the generated sources and `spring.xml` outside the project's source and resource directories, e.g. through a symlinked package.

Both build on a small new `PathConfinement` helper, so the rules live in one place.

Archives built by AMPS itself, such as those from `atlas-create-home-zip`, keep working. Hand-made archives containing links or absolute paths now fail with an error naming the offending entry, so the [docs PR](https://bitbucket.org/atlassian-developers/atlassian-sdk-docs/pull-requests/402) adds a note about what `productDataPath` archives must contain.

One deliberate limit: a process concurrently modifying the target directory could still race the checks. Closing that would need directory-handle APIs that aren't available on Windows, and AMPS only extracts into build directories that should not be writable by untrusted users anyway.
